summary: Provides a many-to-many label store and query API that any object-bearing application can use to attach, remove, search, and group objects by named labels.

classification.why_platform: Labels are a reusable classification primitive with no domain meaning — the same attach/remove/search/group capability applies equally to tasks, meals, workouts, or any other object type registered in the system. No workflow rules, status transitions, or business-specific behaviour live here.
non_goals: serving Dataset-shaped responses directly to the Atlas Shell UI
owning or understanding the domain meaning of attached objects

consumes: Shared Postgres instance (02_Platform/Postgres) via ATLAS_PG_* environment variables
platform_errorhandling package (02_Platform/packages/platform_errorhandling) for structured logging and exception handling
objects.id — the universal object identifier that callers are responsible for registering before attaching labels
provides: Label search by prefix: returns all labels whose name starts with the query string
Label creation: creates a named label, returns the created record
Label attach: idempotently attaches a label to an object by name (creates label inline if absent)
Label remove: removes a specific label from a specific object
Labels for object: returns all labels attached to a given object, ordered by attachment time ascending
Grouped object query: returns objects grouped by their primary label (first-attached), with an Unlabeled group last, scoped by object_type
invariants: A (object_id, label_id) pair is unique — duplicate attachments are silently ignored (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING)
label.name must be a non-empty string after stripping whitespace
primary label is always the label with the smallest attached_at for that object_id — ties broken by label_id ascending
Unlabeled group always appears last in grouped responses
Groups within a grouped response are ordered alphabetically by label name
The labels schema is isolated in its own Postgres schema named 'labels' and does not reference tables in other schemas

object_type values are case-sensitive and must be lowercase (e.g., 'task', not 'Task'). Callers are responsible for supplying a lowercase value. LabelEngine does not normalize casing on write or read.
failure_modes: LABEL_NAME_EMPTY — label name is blank after strip; returns 422
OBJECT_NOT_FOUND — object_id does not exist in the caller's domain; LabelEngine does not validate this — callers are responsible for pre-checking object existence
LABEL_NOT_FOUND — label_id supplied to remove endpoint does not exist; returns 404
ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND — (object_id, label_id) pair does not exist when attempting remove; returns 404
DB_UNAVAILABLE — connection pool exhausted or Postgres unreachable; returns 503
OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED — grouped query called without object_type parameter; returns 422

provides: ObjectLabelRecord: { object_id: str, label_id: str, label_name: str, attached_at: str (ISO-8601) }

GroupedObjectsResponse: { meta: { total: int, page: int, page_size: int, page_count: int }, groups: [ { label: str | 'Unlabeled', items: [ { id: str, primary_label: str | null, labels: list[str] } ] } ] }
HTTP API mounted at /api prefix — all routes listed in exposed_surfaces

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Search labels by name prefix. Query param: q (string, optional). Match is case-insensitive prefix — e.g., q=out matches 'Outside'. Uses ix_labels_name_lower index. Returns LabelSearchResponse.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Create a new label. Body: { name: str }. Returns LabelRecord. Raises LABEL_NAME_EMPTY on blank name.

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Attach a label to an object by name. Body: { label_name: str }. Creates label if absent. Idempotent on duplicate. Returns ObjectLabelRecord for the attachment.

exposed_surfaces.name: DELETE /api/objects/{object_id}/labels/{label_id}
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Remove a label from an object. Raises ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND if the pair does not exist.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return all labels attached to the given object, ordered by attached_at ascending. Returns ObjectLabelsResponse.

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/groups
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Return objects grouped by primary label for a given object_type. Query params: object_type (required), page (optional, default 1), page_size (optional, default 50). Returns GroupedObjectsResponse. Raises OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED if object_type is absent.

internal_flow.name: request_received
internal_flow.description: FastAPI receives HTTP request. platform_errorhandling middleware logs request and installs structured exception handlers.
outputs: validated path/query/body parameters via Pydantic models

internal_flow.name: label_name_validation
internal_flow.description: For endpoints that accept a label name, strip whitespace and raise LABEL_NAME_EMPTY (422) if the result is empty. Applies to POST /api/labels and POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels.
outputs: normalized label_name string or 422 error response

internal_flow.name: label_resolution
internal_flow.description: For the attach endpoint: query labels table for an exact case-insensitive match on name. If found, use existing label_id. If not found, INSERT new label and return generated id. This is the inline creation path.

internal_flow.name: attachment_write
internal_flow.description: For the attach endpoint: INSERT INTO labels.object_labels (object_id, label_id, attached_at) with ON CONFLICT (object_id, label_id) DO NOTHING. attached_at is set to now() on first insert; ignored on conflict.
outputs: ObjectLabelRecord for the (object_id, label_id) pair, whether newly inserted or pre-existing

internal_flow.name: primary_label_resolution
internal_flow.description: For the grouped query endpoint: for each object_id in scope, determine the primary label by selecting the object_labels row with the minimum attached_at (ties broken by label_id ASC). Objects with no labels are assigned to the Unlabeled group.
inputs: all labels.object_labels rows for matching objects
outputs: map of object_id -> primary_label_name, object_id -> all_label_names

internal_flow.name: group_assembly
internal_flow.description: For the grouped query endpoint: assemble GroupedObjectsResponse. Pagination is applied to the flat object list before grouping: the total matching object count is counted first, then the page slice (offset/limit) is taken from the ordered flat list, then those objects are grouped. total in meta = total matching objects for the given object_type (unpaginated). page_count = ceil(total / page_size). Sort named groups alphabetically by label name. Append Unlabeled group last.

internal_flow.name: error_serialization
internal_flow.description: All failure modes produce a JSONResponse matching the R-CON-BP-04 ApiError envelope: { error: { code, message, detail, request_id } }. platform_errorhandling.api_error helper is used.
outputs: JSONResponse with appropriate HTTP status code

internal_required.role: persistent storage for labels and object_labels tables
structured logging, exception handler installation, api_error helper

internal_optional.role: ApiError shape reference — not imported directly; LabelEngine uses api_error helper from platform_errorhandling which already wraps this shape

forbidden: Any import from 03_Application — dependency direction violation per R-CON-PL-02
Domain-specific workflow logic (task status transitions, workout rules, etc.)
Direct Dataset construction for UI — GroupedObjectsResponse is consumed by application backends, not the Atlas Shell directly

persistence.notes: Owns 'labels' schema with two tables: labels.labels and labels.object_labels. The object_labels table includes attached_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now() to support the primary-label ordering invariant (first-attached rule). This column was absent from the draft data model and is added here to satisfy the ordering invariant.

Implement app/service.py: all label business logic — search, create, attach (with inline creation), remove, get-for-object, grouped-query with primary-label resolution
Implement app/routers/groups.py: GET /api/groups with object_type required param
Implement app/main.py: FastAPI app, CORS middleware (localhost regex), mount all routers at /api prefix, startup event calling init_pool + init_schema
Implement Dockerfile following LinkingEngine pattern exactly
Implement compose.yml: bind to 127.0.0.1:8050:8000, atlas-net external network, ATLAS_PG_* env vars, log volume
Implement pyproject.toml: project name label_engine, same dependency set as LinkingEngine

Implement pagination for GET /api/groups using paginate-items-before-grouping model: count total matching objects, apply page/page_size offset to the flat ordered list, then group. Populate meta.total, meta.page, meta.page_size, meta.page_count in GroupedObjectsResponse.
Label name matching on attach: decide case-insensitive exact match or case-sensitive — document the choice; case-insensitive is recommended for UX consistency
ui_implementer: Label picker component (shared between task detail view and task list three-dot menu): text input with live search calling GET /api/labels?q=, Create 'X' option when no match, chip display with remove button
Task detail view: Labels section rendering chips for each label, + Add label button opening the label picker
Task list three-dot menu: Set Labels action opening compact label picker

Task list grouped view: consume GET /api/groups?object_type=task and render section headers by label name, Unlabeled last — this endpoint is consumed via TaskTracker's backend proxy, not called directly from the UI
Note: the Atlas Shell UI must not call LabelEngine endpoints directly — TaskTracker backend proxies all label operations and serves Dataset-shaped responses to the UI where the UI contract applies
test_writer: POST /api/labels: happy path creates label and returns LabelRecord; blank name returns 422 LABEL_NAME_EMPTY
GET /api/labels?q=: returns labels matching prefix; empty q returns all labels; no match returns empty list
POST /api/objects/{object_id}/labels: attaches existing label by name; creates new label inline and attaches; duplicate attach is idempotent (no error, no duplicate row)
DELETE /api/objects/{object_id}/labels/{label_id}: removes existing attachment; returns 404 ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND when pair absent
GET /api/objects/{object_id}/labels: returns labels in attached_at ascending order; returns empty list for object with no labels

GET /api/groups?object_type=task: groups are alphabetical by label name; Unlabeled always last; object with multiple labels appears under first-attached label only; object with no labels appears in Unlabeled; missing object_type param returns 422 OBJECT_TYPE_REQUIRED
Primary-label tie-breaking: two labels attached at same timestamp are broken by label_id ASC
DB_UNAVAILABLE: all write endpoints return 503 when pool exhausted
Label name normalisation: leading/trailing whitespace is stripped before persistence and before name matching

Verify case-sensitivity decision for label name matching is documented
Verify Dockerfile build context matches LinkingEngine pattern (repo root context, platform_packages copy)
Verify labels schema does not reference linking schema tables or any other schema cross-reference

deferred_decisions: Pagination granularity for GET /api/groups: RESOLVED — paginate items before grouping. total = total matching objects for the given object_type (unpaginated count). page_count = ceil(total / page_size). See internal_flow[6] and GroupedObjectsResponse in shared_views.
Label name case sensitivity for search and inline creation matching. Case-insensitive is recommended but not mandated here.
Whether GET /api/groups should accept additional filter params (e.g. label_id to scope a single group) — deferred to a later sprint.
Label deletion endpoint (remove a label entirely, cascading detach from all objects) — not in scope for Sprint01.

risks.impact: TaskTracker backend must transform GroupedObjectsResponse into per-group Datasets before serving the UI. If TaskTracker implementer calls LabelEngine directly from the frontend, the UI data contract (R-CON-BP-04) is violated. This must be enforced at review.

Two labels attached in the same transaction get the same attached_at. The label_id ASC tiebreaker produces a deterministic but arbitrary ordering in this case. For UX correctness, the implementer should ensure attach operations for distinct labels are not batched in a single transaction.

risks.risk: object_id is a foreign concept — LabelEngine does not validate object existence
risks.impact: Orphaned label attachments (labels pointing to deleted objects) will persist. Callers are responsible for cleanup. A later sprint may add a cascade-delete hook or a cleanup job.
Port 8050 is proposed for LabelEngine. If another service already uses 8050 on the host, compose will fail at startup. Reviewer must verify no collision exists.

open_questions.question: Is port 8050 free on the Atlas host, or should a different port be assigned?
Should label name matching on inline creation be case-insensitive (recommended) or case-sensitive? This affects whether 'outside' and 'Outside' become one label or two.
Should GET /api/groups paginate objects before grouping, or paginate the group list itself?
open_questions.owner: RESOLVED — paginate objects before grouping. See deferred_decisions[0] and internal_flow[6].

open_questions.question: Should LabelEngine expose a health endpoint (GET /health) consistent with other platform services?

_resolved_orchestrator_questions.service_topology: Standalone FastAPI service, identical pattern to LinkingEngine. Separate Dockerfile, compose.yml, port binding, and pyproject.toml. Not embedded in any existing service. Evidence: LinkingEngine is a standalone service at port 8040 with its own Dockerfile and compose.yml. LabelEngine follows the same structural pattern.
_resolved_orchestrator_questions.dataset_contract_for_grouped_endpoint: GroupedObjectsResponse is NOT a Dataset. LabelEngine is a platform backend service — it does not serve the Atlas Shell UI directly. The UI data contract (R-CON-BP-04) applies to endpoints consumed by the UI. GET /api/groups is consumed by the TaskTracker application backend, which is responsible for transforming the response into Dataset shape before exposing it to the UI. No exception to R-CON-BP-04 is required; the boundary is correctly placed. LabelEngine exposes GroupedObjectsResponse as a typed backend-to-backend contract.
_resolved_orchestrator_questions.primary_label_ordering: Added attached_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now() to labels.object_labels. Primary label = row with MIN(attached_at) for that object_id. Ties broken by label_id ASC for full determinism. This column is absent from the draft and is a required addition. See schema.sql.
